system: IBM Carbon Design System — Spacing layer (@carbon/layout package: spacing scale, fluid spacing, container/size/icon-size/border-radius primitives, deprecated layout scale, 2x Grid)
sourcesFailed: mcp__github repo-content browsing: 'GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session' — worked around via raw.githubusercontent.com + a WebFetch of the GitHub tree page instead of the API.

packages/layout/style-dictionary/formats/scss-layout.js and js-icon-size/other formatter files — not fetched (time-boxed); js-layout.js alone was enough to confirm the miniUnits/rem math but I did not verify the exact generated SCSS map syntax.

No separate 'fluid spacing usage guidance' page found beyond the 4 token values + one-line description each in src/dtcg/layout.json — could not confirm a fuller rationale doc exists elsewhere in Carbon's docs.
unit: rem is the default output unit for nearly everything — spacing-01…13, size-xs…2xl, icon-size-01…02 and most border-radius steps are all computed at build time as (miniUnit-multiple × 8px) ÷ 16px root, or (raw px) ÷ 16px root, via one shared to-rem() function with a configurable $base-font-size (16px !default). Two edge tokens stay literal px because rem is meaningless there (border-radius-00: "0px", border-radius-max: "999999px" for pill shapes). fluid-spacing-02…04 are vw (viewport-width %), not rem/px/clamp() at all. JS exports mirror the same rem *strings* (e.g. spacing01 = '0.125rem'), not raw px numbers — px only ever appears in prose/descriptions, never as a shipped unit for the main scale.

scale.generator: Not a constant ratio/modular scale — a hand-tuned interleave over one atomic 8px 'mini unit'. Steps 01–03 are fractions of the mini-unit (0.25×, 0.5×, 1× = 2/4/8px, for sub-grid fine adjustments); steps 04–13 alternate 'half-step' and 'whole-step' multiples of it (1.5,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12,20 × 8px). Source of truth is one DTCG JSON file (src/dtcg/layout.json) with an explicit $extensions.carbon.layout.converter:'miniUnits' on each token; a Style-Dictionary build (sd.config.js) turns that single file into scss/generated/*.scss + js/generated/layout-tokens.(js|d.ts) — nobody hand-authors the numbers twice.
scale.base: 8px 'mini unit' (= 1 mini-unit = 0.5rem @ 16px root); confirmed three independent ways in the sources: the 2x-Grid docs prose ('the 8-pixel square mini unit'), the Sizing-scale table (8px = 1x, 16px = 2x … 80px = 10x), and the js-layout.js formatter's own constant `const MINI_UNIT = 8;`.
scale.notes: These 13 values are byte-identical to the long-standing Carbon v10 Sass scale (cross-checked against docs/migration/10.x-layout.md's $spacing-01…09/$spacing-3xs…3xl mapping table) even though the whole authoring pipeline was rewritten from hand-written Sass to a DTCG/Style-Dictionary JSON source in 2026 — i.e. the scale itself has been treated as immutable across a full architecture migration; only the machinery around it changed. Sibling primitive families exist for jobs the spacing scale is NOT meant for: container-01…05 (interactive-element height: 24/32/40/48/64px) and size-xs…2xl (named component size: 24/32/40/48/64/80px) — both their own small ladders, not spacing steps reused.

vocabulary: spacing-01…13 (general spacing scale, used directly in component/page code)
layout-01…07 — DEPRECATED, 'Replaced by the spacing scale — do not use in new work'
examples: spacing-05 — 'Standard spacing unit; use for typical component padding and gutters.' (16px)
spacing-09 — 'Use for large vertical rhythm and section separation.' (48px)
spacing-13 — 'Use for the largest page-level spacing needs.' (160px)
roles.notes: Unlike Carbon's color tokens (primitive → semantic role → component, enforced structurally so a component never reads a raw palette value), spacing has ONE layer: docs and code consume $spacing-05 etc. directly — there is no $spacing-card-padding or $spacing-section-gap semantic indirection in the core package. Each per-token $description in the DTCG source acts as prose usage-guidance ('use for X') instead of a second named token. Carbon DID once try a second full numeric scale for macro/page-level jobs (layout-01…07, for the exact 'воздух vs поля' split this research is for) — and explicitly deprecated it back into the single spacing scale rather than keep two ladders in sync.

density: No token-level density switch for the spacing scale itself — spacing-01…13 do not change value in any documented 'compact' mode. The one primary-source density lever found is at the grid, not the token: docs/migration/10.x-layout.md lists `$carbon--grid-gutter--condensed` as a v10-era Sass variable that swaps the grid gutter width. Component-level 'compact'/'condensed' variants (e.g. data table) restyle by picking a smaller spacing-XX step in their own CSS, not via a separate density multiplier applied to the scale.
fluid: Two separate, non-interacting mechanisms — not a clamp() ramp anywhere in this package. (1) The 13-step spacing scale is entirely fixed/discrete: per the spacing FAQ, 'the tokens themselves do not change values based on the screen size,' and responsiveness means swapping which FIXED step you apply inside a media query ('at 1440px padding-right: $spacing-05 but at breakpoint 768px padding-right: $spacing-03') — never interpolating between two numbers. (2) A separate 4-token fluid-spacing-01…04 group (0, 2vw, 5vw, 10vw, from src/dtcg/layout.json) exists purely for full-bleed/hero sections, expressed as raw viewport-width percentages with NO clamp(), no min floor and no max ceiling — confirmed in js-layout.js's resolveValue(), which passes the vw string straight through with no bounding logic. At 320px wide, fluid-spacing-04 is 32px; at 2880px wide it is 288px — genuinely unbounded.
layout: No separate 'page rhythm' token family (top/gap/bottom for a section band) survives in the current system — that job used to be the layout-01…07 scale (16/24/32/48/64/96/160px, i.e. the same numbers as spacing-05/06/07/09/10/12/13) and is now explicitly deprecated in favor of applying spacing-XX directly. What DOES carry fixed layout numbers is the 2x Grid itself: 5 named breakpoints (Small 320px/20rem·4 cols, Medium 672px/42rem·8 cols, Large 1056px/66rem·16 cols, X-Large 1312px/82rem·16 cols, Max 1584px/99rem·16 cols), each with its own margin (0/16/16/16/24px) while padding stays a constant 16px (= spacing-05) at every single breakpoint, and gutter is a fixed 32px total (= spacing-07, from doubling the 16px margin) — 'the margin around each grid box matches its padding, for a total gutter of 32 pixels.'
enforcement: Architectural single-source-of-truth + generated build output, not a runtime/CI linter. packages/layout/src/dtcg/layout.json (W3C Design Tokens Community Group format) is the ONLY place values are authored; a Style Dictionary config (style-dictionary/sd.config.js) reads that one file and writes scss/generated/*.scss + js/generated/layout-tokens.(js|d.ts) — and packages/layout/.gitignore lists 'generated', so the build output isn't even committed, closing off hand-editing by construction (first rebuild would silently discard any manual edit). The docs' only enforcement language is advisory prose ('deviating from the spacing scales should be avoided whenever possible') — I found no automated stylelint-style rule in what I read that rejects a raw px/rem value in Carbon component code the way this project's lint:css rejects raw !important/duplicate selectors; the guardrail is that only the ~17 named exports exist to reach for, not a check that blocks reaching around them.

principles.principle: The whole scale is generated from ONE atomic base unit (8px mini-unit) via two multiplier rules, never hand-typed as 13 independent numbers.
principles.evidence: 'The basic unit of 2x Grid geometry is the 8-pixel square mini unit' (elements/2x-grid/overview/); src/dtcg/layout.json: spacing-01 $value 0.25 with converter 'miniUnits' → 0.25×8=2px.
principles.forStorefront3: Give storefront3's spacing tokens one base-unit constant too and derive every step from it in a single generator file (JSON/TS → CSS custom properties + the admin design-snapshot.mjs slepok), the same discipline CLAUDE.md's rule 0 ('Против заплаток') already demands and that token-layer.test.ts already enforces for color — add an equivalent spacing generator + guard instead of 13 hand-typed clamp()/px literals scattered across CSS files.

principles.principle: Spacing primitives are consumed directly in components — Carbon has NO semantic spacing layer analogous to its color primitive→role→component chain.
principles.evidence: DTCG source groups are spacing/fluid-spacing/container/size/icon-size/border-radius/layout only — no 'semantic' group; docs' own code examples call $spacing-05 directly, never through a role alias.
principles.forStorefront3: Don't force-fit the palette pattern (palette→semantic→component, held by token-layer.test.ts) onto spacing. Keep ONE primitive spacing scale file, and let the small number of named layout roles CLAUDE.md already requires (--layout-band-pad, --layout-band-gap, --layout-rail-pad-*) be thin, explicitly-listed aliases straight onto specific primitive steps — not a second full parallel scale, and not a per-component semantic token the way brandTheme colors get.

principles.principle: Carbon tried a second numeric scale for macro/page-level gaps (layout-01…07) and explicitly deprecated it back into the single spacing scale rather than maintain two ladders.
principles.evidence: src/dtcg/layout.json, 'layout' group: '$description: Deprecated layout scale tokens. Replaced by the spacing scale — do not use in new work.' on every layout-0X token.
principles.forStorefront3: This is a direct warning for the 'поля vs воздух' split this research was commissioned for: keep 'поля' (padding) and 'воздух' (band rhythm) as two ROLE vocabularies, but pull both from the SAME one primitive spacing scale/registry (sit it next to the existing packages/ui/src/tokens/seams.ts) — never give 'воздух' its own independently-numbered ladder the way Carbon once did and had to walk back.

principles.principle: The scale is fixed per breakpoint, not continuously interpolated — 'responsive spacing' in Carbon means switching to a different fixed step inside a media query, never a formula between two numbers.
principles.evidence: Spacing FAQ: 'No, the tokens themselves do not change values based on the screen size... it is acceptable at page breakpoints to jump a step(s)... (i.e., at 1440px padding-right: $spacing-05 but at breakpoint 768px padding-right: $spacing-03).'
principles.forStorefront3: storefront3's own rule for the 861–1440 seam (CLAUDE.md, 'Широкая раскладка сжимается') already goes further than Carbon by using clamp() ramps instead of a hard breakpoint jump — treat that as a deliberate, already-decided improvement, not a gap; just make sure the clamp() endpoints themselves are primitive-scale numbers (spacing-XX values) pulled from the same registry, not independently eyeballed pixel numbers.

principles.principle: A genuinely fluid/viewport-relative group exists (fluid-spacing-01…04 = 0/2vw/5vw/10vw) but it is deliberately simple and UNCLAMPED — no min floor, no max ceiling.
principles.evidence: src/dtcg/layout.json fluid-spacing values are bare vw strings; style-dictionary/formats/js-layout.js's resolveValue() passes non-miniUnit/non-rem values through unchanged (no clamp/min/max logic anywhere in that formatter).
principles.forStorefront3: Do NOT copy the bare-vw approach for any storefront3 fluid gap — CLAUDE.md already mandates clamp(minimum, ramp, число_из_макета) for exactly the failure mode a bare vw has (no floor at 320px, no ceiling above 1440px, as documented in DECISIONS.md's ramp discussions). If a full-bleed hero gap is ever wanted, it's Carbon's 'proportional gap' idea PLUS the clamp() guard storefront3's own rules already require — never vw alone.

principles.principle: Component/target sizing (container-01…05, size-xs…2xl) is its own small primitive family, deliberately NOT derived from the 8px spacing ladder, because 44px-class touch targets don't land cleanly on 8px multiples.
principles.evidence: src/dtcg/layout.json 'container' group (24/32/40/48/64px, converter miniUnits ×8) and 'size' group (24/32/40/48/64/80px, converter 'rem' i.e. raw px) are separate token groups from 'spacing'.
principles.forStorefront3: This validates the project's existing roundSm(44)/roundMd(48)/roundLg(72) control-size ladder in CLAUDE.md's 'Кнопка отвечает одинаково' section as the right pattern, not a special case to reconcile with the spacing scale — keep touch-target sizing as its own small named scale, the way Carbon keeps container-* separate from spacing-*, instead of trying to make 44px a spacing-scale step.

principles.principle: One authored source file + a build step generates every downstream artifact (SCSS vars, JS constants, .d.ts types); the generated output is .gitignore'd so it structurally cannot be hand-edited without being silently overwritten.
principles.evidence: style-dictionary/sd.config.js: source: [DTCG_SOURCE] → writes scss/generated/ and js/generated/; packages/layout/.gitignore contains the single line 'generated'.
principles.forStorefront3: Mirror this exactly for spacing the way it's already done for color (design-snapshot.mjs + design-snapshot.test.ts): one authored spacing token file → a generator writes the CSS custom properties AND feeds the admin Design-system screen's slepok, with a sentinel test that fails if the generated file is stale — same shape as token-layer.test.ts, applied to spacing instead of palette.

doNotCopy: Carbon's fluid-spacing (2vw/5vw/10vw) is unclamped — copying it verbatim would violate storefront3's own already-written clamp() rule (no floor/ceiling), which exists precisely to prevent this failure mode.

Carbon's 5 grid breakpoints (320/672/1056/1312/1584) don't match storefront3's seam registry (860 shop seam, 1440 Figma reference) — take the discipline (named, registered breakpoints), not the specific pixel values.

Carbon exposes spacing primitives with literally no semantic layer; don't read that as license to skip naming roles for storefront3's 'поля'/'воздух' split — Carbon's own history (deprecating layout-01…07) argues against a SECOND full numeric scale, not against a handful of named aliases onto one scale.

Don't paste Carbon's 13 px numbers as if they were universal law — they're derived from Carbon's own 8px mini-unit and 16px root; if storefront3 picks a different base unit or root size, every step must be re-derived from that base, not copied as literals.

Carbon's 'acceptable to jump a step at breakpoints' FAQ answer describes a coarser, hard-breakpoint model than what storefront3 already committed to (clamp() ramps across 861–1440) — don't regress storefront3's spacing to breakpoint-jump behavior citing this as 'how Carbon does it.'

quotes.text: The basic unit of 2x Grid geometry is the 8-pixel square mini unit.
The Carbon spacing scale complements the 2x Grid and typography scale by using multiples of two, four, and eight.
No, the tokens themselves do not change values based on the screen size.
it is acceptable at page breakpoints to jump a step(s) on the spacing scale to fit spacing needs
Deprecated layout token — 16px. Replaced by spacing scale. Do not use in new work.
Padding is always a fixed multiple of mini units: 16 pixels at all standard breakpoints.
There are always exceptions to the rule, but deviating from the spacing scales should be avoided whenever possible.
Fluid spacing token — 10vw. Use for large fluid spacing in full-bleed or hero sections.

confidence: High for all numeric values (spacing-01…13, fluid-spacing-01…04, container-*, size-*): read directly from the primary DTCG token source (src/dtcg/layout.json) and independently cross-checked against three other sources that all agree — the public docs site's live scss/js API tables, the historical v9→v10 migration table, and the js-layout.js formatter's own MINI_UNIT=8/BASE_FONT_SIZE=16 constants. Medium for governance/enforcement claims: the Style-Dictionary pipeline and .gitignore'd output are directly verified facts, but the claim 'no automated lint against raw px in component code' is an absence inferred from what I could read in the time available, not from an exhaustive search of the whole carbon-components-react/web-components source. Medium-low for the 'no fuller fluid-spacing rationale doc' claim, since I did not search IBM Products / other Carbon-adjacent doc sites beyond carbondesignsystem.com and the core carbon repo.
